title: Resolving the H0 and S8 Tensions Through Local-Global Inference Separation: An Energy-Flow Cosmology Analysis
description: Introduces an Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) mechanism that separates local and global inference using an entropy-dependent mapping, resolving both the H0 and S8 tensions without altering the cosmic expansion history, sound horizon, or early-universe physics. The paper demonstrates a ∆χ2 = 40.29 improvement for H0 consistency and reduces the S8 tension from 3.3σ to 0.3σ while remaining consistent with BAO, SNe Ia, and CMB constraints.
author: Morten Magnusson

energy_flow_potential.description: Defines the Energy-Flow potential coupling matter density to a dimensionless entropy field S in [0,1].

mean_entropy_evolution.description: Phenomenological evolution of the cosmic-mean entropy with asymptote S_∞ and timescale a_S.

modified_friedmann.description: Background expansion including an entropy-sector energy density contribution Ω_S(z).

entropy_density_contribution.description: Parametrization of the entropy-sector contribution to the expansion as a function of mean entropy.

effective_gravitational_coupling.description: Entropy-dependent effective Newton constant; negative β suppresses late-time structure growth.

local_entropy.description: Environmental modulation of entropy by local matter overdensity δ_m with coupling γ_S.

local_h0_inference.description: Bias in locally inferred H0 when interpreting data assuming cosmic-average entropy.

modified_growth.description: Linear growth with entropy-induced damping (η) and modified strength via β.

halo_entropy_profile.description: Spherically symmetric entropy profile for galactic halos transitioning over scale r_S.

effective_potential_galaxies.description: Entropy-coupled effective gravitational potential at galactic scales; α consistent with cosmological β.

key_results.main_finding: An entropy-dependent local-global inference separation within EFC simultaneously resolves the H0 and S8 tensions without altering H(z), r_d, or early-universe physics, remaining consistent with BAO, SNe Ia, and CMB.

sealed_predictions.statement: After controlling for calibration and selection systematics, locally inferred H0 residuals will anti-correlate with smoothed large-scale matter overdensity δ_m on 20–50 Mpc scales with slope consistent with γ_S ≈ 0.20 (i.e., underdense regions yield higher H0).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Cross-correlation of H0 residual maps from SNe Ia/Cepheid calibrators with reconstructed density fields from galaxy surveys (e.g., DESI, SDSS) at 20–50 Mpc smoothing.

sealed_predictions.statement: The late-time amplitude of matter fluctuations is S8(z≈0) = 0.766 ± 0.020 with β = −0.08 and η = 0.05.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Stage-III/IV weak-lensing and galaxy–galaxy lensing measurements (e.g., KiDS, DES, HSC, Euclid, Rubin-LSST) combined with clustering and CMB lensing.

sealed_predictions.statement: BAO and CMB acoustic scales, including the sound horizon r_d and CMB peak positions, remain unchanged relative to ΛCDM within current uncertainties.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI BAO distance ladder and Planck/Simons Observatory/CMB-S4 acoustic scale measurements showing statistically significant shifts in r_d or peak positions.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galaxy-scale coupling α inferred from rotation curves is consistent in sign with cosmological β (<0) and within a factor of ≲2 in magnitude when mapped via S(r).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint fits to large SPARC samples and independent rotation-curve datasets comparing α to β from growth data.

kill_criteria: KC1: No negative correlation between local H0 residuals and large-scale overdensity δ_m is observed at ≥2σ when analyzed on 20–50 Mpc smoothing scales; specifically, dH0/dδ_m ≥ 0 or |γ_S| < 0.05 in joint SN+density-field analyses would falsify the local-global inference mechanism.

KC2: Combined growth measurements (RSD, weak lensing, CMB lensing) in 0 < z < 1 statistically exclude β < 0 at ≥95% CL (i.e., favor β ≥ 0 or |β| ≪ 0.02), contradicting the required late-time growth suppression.

KC3: High-precision BAO and CMB analyses detect a shift in the sound horizon r_d or acoustic peak positions inconsistent with ΛCDM at >1% that cannot be absorbed by inference effects (the model asserts r_d and early-universe physics are unchanged).

KC4: Type Ia SN Hubble diagram and cosmic chronometer data require a modified H(z) at z < 1 beyond ΛCDM at >1% level to reconcile datasets, violating the paper’s assumption that the expansion history is unchanged and only inference is modified.

KC5: A comprehensive SPARC/rotation-curve fit demands a galaxy-scale coupling α with sign opposite to β or a magnitude irreconcilable with the cosmological β (e.g., |α/β| ≫ 2 or α > 0 with β < 0) at ≥3σ, breaking cross-regime coherence.
KC6: Next-generation weak-lensing surveys robustly measure S8(z≈0) ≥ 0.82 ± 0.01, inconsistent with the EFC-predicted late-time suppression to S8 ≈ 0.766 under the calibrated parameters.
name: EFC-H0-S8-Tensions
abstract: The Hubble tension and S8 tension represent the most significant challenges to ΛCDM. We present an analysis within the EFC framework demonstrating that both tensions can be resolved simultaneously through entropy-dependent modification of local-to-global parameter inference.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper is the first dedicated EFC empirical analysis resolving both the H0 and S8 tensions simultaneously via entropy-dependent local-global inference separation, achieving Δχ²=40.29 for H0 and reducing S8 tension from 3.3σ to 0.3σ. It does not alter H(z), r_d, or early-universe physics, preserving full BAO/SNe/CMB consistency. It establishes five paper-level kill criteria and four sealed predictions that map directly onto the Stage-IV KC framework, strengthening the empirical backbone of EFC without closing any Stage-IV KC outright since those require independent external data confirmation.
graph_insights: This paper is currently an orphan node in the knowledge graph (no 1-2 hop connections found), which is anomalous given it touches H0, S8, BAO, CMB, weak lensing, and SPARC — all of which should have extensive existing graph presence. This suggests the graph ingestion for prior EFC papers may be incomplete, or the concept-matching thresholds are too strict. Recommend re-indexing existing papers against this paper's concept set.

The paper creates a natural bridge node between the galaxy-scale EFC sector (SPARC, rotation curves) and the cosmological-scale sector (H0, S8, BAO, CMB). Once graph connections are established, it should have high betweenness centrality — it is the first paper to formally link these two regimes through cross-regime coherence (KC5/P4).

The absence of validation tests sharing observables in the graph query is surprising given 119 total tests exist. The H0 and S8 observables must already appear in existing tests. This paper should be connected to any existing weak lensing, RSD, BAO, or SN consistency tests.

implicit_consequences: The sealed prediction P2 (S8=0.766±0.020) directly feeds the DESI DR2 fσ8 rapid-response pipeline: if DESI DR2 full-shape analysis at z=0.7 returns fσ8 consistent with EFC's growth suppression (β<0), it simultaneously validates this paper's S8 prediction and the existing sealed prediction (fσ8=0.430). These are now linked validation chains.

Paper KC2 (late-time growth β<0) and the existing sealed fσ8 prediction share the same observable space: any DESI/Euclid/Rubin growth measurement that tests one necessarily constrains the other. The rapid-response pipeline (current biggest gap) now has double motivation.

The local-global inference separation mechanism implies that any future high-precision local H0 measurement must be accompanied by a density-field characterization of the measurement volume — this creates a new systematic requirement for SH0ES-like programs.

If P1 (H0-δ_m anti-correlation) is confirmed by upcoming peculiar velocity surveys or SN+density cross-correlations, it would independently validate the entropy-field gradient mechanism at the core of all EFC predictions, not just the tensions paper.

The paper's insistence that H(z) and r_d are unchanged means EFC now occupies a unique niche: it is not early dark energy, not modified gravity in the traditional sense, and not a systematic error claim — it is an inference-layer modification. This has implications for how EFC should be classified in comparison papers and meta-analyses.

Cross-regime coherence (P4/KC5 linking SPARC α to cosmological β) means the galaxy rotation curve fits and cosmological tension resolution are not independent tests — a single future SPARC analysis could simultaneously validate or falsify both the galaxy-scale and cosmological-scale EFC sectors.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_change: The biggest gap remains the DESI DR2 full-shape RSD rapid-response pipeline, but this paper now adds urgency: the S8 sealed prediction (S8=0.766±0.020) and the growth-suppression kill criterion (β<0) are both directly testable by the same pipeline. The gap description should note that the pipeline now serves dual purpose — validating both the fσ8 sealed prediction and the tensions-paper S8/growth predictions.
